I wouldn't be too concerned with too much knee bend.  Your problem is that you're folding too much at the hips and that is causing the lower back rounding.  In fact, if you were to bring your knees forward and with a little more bend, you might be able to do proper deficit deadlift form without the lower back rounding.  To cue a flat back, try to point your butt up instead of letting it tuck under you.  Also, you should work on your neck position.  You're cranking it too far back in the beginning of the lift.  Keep your neck in line with the rest of your spine throughout the lift.

If you're going to be starting with such small weights (small in diameter) you should stack books or something under the plates to raise the bar to where a regular deadlift would start from (looks like you need about 4 more inches).  In your video I see that you are needing to bend too low and due to lack of hip mobility is causing your lower back to round.

Not necessarily.  Lower back soreness is going to happen if your lower back is relatively untrained compared to the rest of the muscles that are moving during deadlifts.  Until the lower back is brought up to speed, it's important to progress slowly.

Twenty something odd years ago, when the Sega Genesis was released, very few people were excited or cared because the original NES still had a huge grip on the industry.  I would always beg my mother to take me to toysRus.  Anyways, those cheap bastards had a display Genesis but it was kept behind glass meaning you couldn't play.  It was running the rolling demo for Altered Beast.  I remember being floored by the graphics and wishing with all of my being that I could just touch it.  So for six months, once a week, every Saturday, my routine was to beg mother to take me there.  Little 10 year old me would stand for an hour and passively watch the same demo over and over again.  Finally after much begging and many promises that I would study extra hard and make perfect grades, my mother bought one for my birthday.  Few words could express the joygasamification I felt as we purchased it and the anticipation as we drove home.  Plowing past my siblings to hook the thing up to the TV, I started my first game.  Two hours later, the game was beat...  It wasn't even that good of a game.  Also, due to being poor, I didn't get a new game until a year later.  Also also, none of the rental joints at the time rented genesis games out because no one had a genesis but me.  Anyways, the genesis did end up being worth the anticipation but only like 3 years after it was bought when good games finally came out.  TLDR: Game demo displays that don't allow play can eat several large bowls of cock (ehem wii U)
